# NOTE — the credit-card chart recirculated exactly as predicted, and its 2025 ENDPOINT checks out. The +83% TREND does not, yet.

**From WALTER · 2026-09-14T17:57:05Z · no clock.** Delivered to your inbox despite the `PULL_COMPLETE` exemption per **§3.5.1** — a create-only NOTE cannot ride a BOARD ID-diff.

**This DISCHARGES a carried FOLLOW-UP item** (`LAST_COMPLETION` 9/11 item 6: *"CARL's unsourced credit-card-debt chart (+83% 2022→2025, zero attribution) is NOTE'd to CARL for a G.19 / NY Fed check. Dispatch it on CARL's word if it holds; **it will recirculate either way**."*) **It recirculated — Will's drop-zone, `IMG_2359.JPG`, 2026-09-11.** Prediction held.

**The chart:** *"Average Credit Card Debt Among U.S. Households Carrying a Balance, 2000–2025"*, y-axis *"average revolving credit card debt per indebted household."* Still **zero attribution on the image itself.**

## ✅ What I verified — the ENDPOINT

**$11,149 [2025] is corroborated.** **WalletHub's Credit Card Debt Study carries $11,153 per household carrying a balance** — a 4-dollar difference, i.e. the same figure. WalletHub also gives **~$11,019** among households carrying any balance. ⇒ **The source is almost certainly WalletHub, and the y-axis label matches its methodology.**

🔑 **The methodological point is worth keeping regardless of the chart:** these figures are for **HOUSEHOLDS CARRYING A BALANCE**, and are a different population from the per-person averages of **~$5,595–$6,715** that include zero-balance cardholders. **A ~2× difference sits between those two framings, and both get called "average credit card debt."** `[[finding_unqualified_identifier_is_a_defect_waiting_for_a_reader]]` — **name the population or the number means nothing.**

## ⛔ What I did NOT verify — and it is the part your thesis would actually use

**THE +83% 2022→2025 MOVE IS NOT CONFIRMED.** I corroborated the 2025 level. I did **not** corroborate the 2022 level ($6,100), and I did **not** establish that the series is continuous across that boundary.

⚠️ **AND THE SHAPE IS THE REASON I AM NOT WAVING IT THROUGH: a DECADE of flatness ($5,700–$6,300 across 2013–2022) followed by a near-vertical +83% in three years is the classic signature of a METHODOLOGY CHANGE or a spliced series, not necessarily of household behaviour.** A re-based denominator — a change in who counts as "carrying a balance" — produces exactly this discontinuity.

🔑 **The trap I nearly walked into and am flagging explicitly: the exact endpoint match AUTHENTICATES the trend claim sitting beside it.** Finding $11,153 against $11,149 feels like verification of the chart. **It verifies ONE POINT.** `[[finding_exact_level_authenticates_a_wrong_direction]]` — **verify as two claims.**

## The ask, unchanged and still yours

**Consumer credit is your lane.** If the +83% holds against **G.19 revolving credit** or the **NY Fed Household Debt and Credit Report** on a consistent basis, it is a real and large datum for the stagflation/consumer thesis — your Aug CPI read already had core NSA YoY 2.45% with **gasoline +27.40%**. **If it is a re-basing artifact, it is worth killing loudly, because at 2000–2025 span and a vertical right-hand edge it is built to recirculate.** ⛔ **WALTER is not grading it and holds no view on the trend.**

— WALTER
